See also: BIP, bíp, and bịp

Translingual

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Clipping of English Bila with p as a placeholder.

Symbol

[edit]

bip

  1. (international standards) ISO 639-3 language code for Bila.

See also

[edit]
  • Wiktionary’s coverage of Bila terms

English

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Imitative.

Verb

[edit]

bip (third-person singular simple present bips, present participle bipping, simple past and past participle bipped)

  1. (informal) To make or cause to make a short beeping or blipping sound.
    • 2011, David Cullen, The Byblos Discovery, page 275:
      Jihad Merhi bipped the horn as he pulled up in his Land Cruiser outside chez Lattouf.
  2. (informal, transitive) To hit lightly.
    Synonyms: bop, boop
    • A. P. Vasko, 33 Miracles (page 188)
      After the entire table burst into laughter, she playfully bipped the man in the mouth and followed it with a kiss.
    • 2003, C. D. Blizzard, Broken:
      I swung the bat, barely bipped the ball, and sent it spinning off into a neighbor's yard. That was the closest I'd come to hitting that thing all day.
  3. (Bay Area, California slang) To break into a car and steal its contents.
    1. (by extension) To rob; steal.
      So many cars get bipped on that street.
      • 1972, Bruce Jackson, In the Life: Versions of the Criminal Experience‎[1], New York, N.Y.; Chicago, I.L.; San Francisco, C.A.: Holt, Rinehart and Winston, →ISBN, page 82:
        Around Christmas of that year me and a friend was going to go up through Oklahoma bipping — scallybipping [burglarizing a house when they saw the wife out back hanging clothes], you know. We had been doing it around Houston, Dallas, places like that, but now we was going to go up through the States.

Translations

[edit]
to hit lightly
  • Galician: chincar, chiscar (gl)
  • Spanish: golpetear (es)

Noun

[edit]

bip (plural bips)

  1. (Bay Area, California slang) Synonym of spliff.
    • 2020 October 10, “Toot That Sh!t Up”, Kai Bandz (lyrics), 1:34:
      My niggas getting greasy with them licks, nigga
      But these free banks, I ain’t use no bip, nigga
    • 2022 March 11, “B$G Intro” (track 1, right in the beginning), in Baby Stone Gorillas (lyrics), BABYST5XNE GORILLAS‎[2]:
      You have your bip on you?
      'Cause if you ain't got no bip on you, I ain't hangin' out with you
  2. (finance) Abbreviation of basis point.
  3. (African-American Vernacular, Baltimore, slang) Can refer to multiple different things, but usually refers to a piece that someone owns, most often a gun or a haircut.

Anagrams

[edit]
  • BPI, PBI, PIB, PiB, pib

Bahnar

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Chamic. Compare Rade bip (“duck”).

The common Bahnaric term for "duck" was *ʔədaː.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /biːp/

Noun

[edit]

bip

  1. duck

Romanian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from English beep.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈbip/
  • Rhymes: -ip

Noun

[edit]

bip n (plural bipuri)

  1. beep
  2. (telephony, colloquial) prearranged missed call
  3. (television) bleep censor
